findings.title: Catalog SQL injection exposes unpublished products
findings.controlled_input: category query parameter; reproduced with books' OR 1=1 --
findings.broken_boundary: Untrusted category text becomes SQL syntax, bypassing the selected-category and published-only filters.
findings.runtime_evidence: The normal books request returned one published book. The injected request returned all three products, including the unpublished draft and the tools product.
findings.remedy: Bind category as a SQL parameter.

findings.title: Signed-in user can retrieve another user's invoice
findings.controlled_input: Invoice ID in the path, with a valid user token
findings.broken_boundary: Authentication succeeds, but the retrieved invoice is never checked against the authenticated owner.
findings.runtime_evidence: No token returned 401; Alice's token returned her invoice 1 and also Bob's invoice 2 with its amount.
findings.remedy: Restrict the invoice lookup to the authenticated owner, or check ownership before returning it.

findings.title: Download path traversal reads private application data
findings.broken_boundary: The path is joined under data/public without enforcing that the resolved file remains there.
findings.runtime_evidence: The normal request returned the public fixture. The traversal request returned the synthetic note from data/internal.
findings.remedy: Resolve the requested path and reject any path outside the resolved public directory.
